Article Title: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal shares an update on Temple device, writes ‘Temple Batch 01 pre orders open …’
Article Text:
Deepinder Goyal has announced six color options for Temple, his upcoming health wearable device

Hand-made units, three-month delivery timeline

What Temple does

The road to launch

Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal has shared a new update on Temple, the hardware venture he has been teasing in recent months, announcing that pre-orders for the first batch of the device will open on November 1. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter), Goyal wrote, “The wait is over. Temple Batch 01 pre orders open November 1. Each @temple is hand-made to order and delivered to you within three months of your purchase." Along with announcing the pre-order date, Goyal also indicated that the company is taking a measured approach to scaling production. According to Goyal, Temple is following a "grow slow" strategy, with a focus on maintaining quality control and ensuring customers receive a strong experience. "Quality control, and also making sure we serve each customer well. Following the 'grow slow' approach with temple," Goyal said while explaining the company's approach to fulfilling orders.The latest update suggests that Temple's first production batch will be manufactured to order rather than mass-produced. Goyal said every unit will be hand-made, with deliveries expected within three months of purchase.The announcement gives potential buyers their first clear timeline for ordering the device, while also signalling that availability may remain limited during the initial phase as the company prioritises production quality over rapid expansion.It will come in six colours, with Real Jade, Deep Blue and Purple Funk marked as limited editions. Temple has not yet announced pricing, the number of devices in the first batch, or the exact date deliveries will begin, and said it would share more information before pre-orders open.Temple is an experimental health-tech wearable developed under a private initiative backed by Goyal. It uses optical sensors to track changes in cerebral blood flow, a metric the company calls BrainFlow. The device tracks blood flow and oxygenation inside the brain. The wearable first drew attention when Goyal appeared on a podcast in early 2026 wearing a small metallic clip-like device on his head.In May, Goyal announced that the first 100 devices were ready to ship to select founding users, including athletes, scientists, doctors, founders and creators. In August, he said the latest version was less than half the size of the one shown earlier, and claimed it was the smallest wearable on the market by volume and the most powerful. Independent reports noted that he gave no hardware specifications or performance data to back that claim. At that time, he said the limited launch edition would ship before the end of 2026. The new three-month delivery window suggests that orders placed from November 1 could reach customers in early 2027.
Article Summary: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal has announced pre-orders for Temple will open on November 1. Goyal said every unit will be hand-made, with deliveries expected within three months of purchase. Temple is an experimental health-tech wearable developed under a private initiative backed by Goyal.

Article Title: UltraProlink launches Juice-Up Mag 7 magnetic wireless power bank in India at Rs 3,499
Article Text: Consumer technology accessories brand UltraProlink has expanded its portable charging portfolio with the launch of the Juice-Up Mag 7, a 10,000mAh magnetic wireless power bank designed for smartphones and other compatible devices. The new power bank combines magnetic wireless charging and wired fast charging in a slim 16.5mm form factor. According to the company, the Juice-Up Mag 7 supports up to 15W magnetic wireless charging, 22.5W USB-C Power Delivery (PD) output and 22W PPS fast charging. The product is aimed at users looking for a travel-friendly charging solution for daily commutes, work and travel.The Juice-Up Mag 7 offers magnetic wireless charging with support for 5W, 7.5W, 10W and 15W charging speeds, depending on the connected device. UltraProlink said the magnetic alignment system is designed to work with compatible smartphones, including supported iPhone, Pixel, Samsung and OnePlus devices. For users seeking faster charging speeds, the power bank also supports up to 22.5W USB-C PD charging. The company claims compatible iPhone models can charge from 0% to 50% in 30 minutes through the USB-C port, although actual performance may vary depending on device, battery condition and usage.The device supports multiple charging standards, including PD 3.0, PD 2.0, PPS, QC 3.0, QC 2.0, AFC, PE 2.0, PE 1.1 and SCP, enabling compatibility across a wide range of smartphones and gadgets.Despite housing a 10,000mAh battery, UltraProlink says the Juice-Up Mag 7 measures just 16.5mm thick, making it suitable for carrying in backpacks, laptop bags and travel pouches. The power bank features an integrated LCD display that shows the remaining battery percentage, allowing users to monitor available charge at a glance. The company also highlighted that the 38.5Wh battery capacity meets flight-safe requirements, making it suitable for air travel.UltraProlink said the power bank is BIS certified and manufactured in India. It also incorporates the company's Safety Shield protection system, which includes safeguards against short circuits, overheating, overcurrent and overcharging.The UltraProlink Juice-Up Mag 7 10,000mAh portable power bank is priced at Rs 3,499 and is available through UltraProlink.com and Amazon.in.
Article Summary: The Juice-Up Mag 7 combines magnetic wireless charging and wired fast charging in a slim 16.5mm form factor. The product is aimed at users looking for a travel-friendly charging solution for daily commutes, work and travel. UltraProlink said the magnetic alignment system is designed to work with compatible smartphones, including supported iPhone, Pixel and Samsung devices.

Article Title: Patch or go offline, say security agencies in the US, UK and Europe to companies as two critical bugs in PHP put millions of websites at risk
Article Text:
Representative Image

FBI to companies in America: Follow these steps right away

UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) to companies: Update to the latest version

European Union's CERT-EU to organisations: Patch affected assets immediately

Several security agencies across the world have sent out an alarming warning that two critical holes have been found in PHP. The critical bugs allow hackers to run code on almost any server running the PHP language. For those unaware, PHP is a server-side programming language widely used for web applications. It is said to power roughly 70% of the websites on the internet. Reports suggest that the details on two critical-severity PHP vulnerabilities named PHP2Shell have been leaked online ahead of scheduled coordinated disclosure and official patches. Public reporting calls the vulnerabilities PHP2Shell, suggesting that attackers could exploit them to obtain shells on vulnerable servers.Following the disclosure, government websites in several parts of Europe, UK and some in the US went offline. The Dutch cybersecurity agency itself went offline, saying it had done so as a precaution because of the vulnerabilities. Disruption was even more widespread in Finland, where state IT services provider Valtori said that the government public network services had been taken offline "as a precautionary measure." France's Interior Ministry said it had placed all of its websites into preventive maintenance.Here's what security agencies across the world are telling companies to do to protect their websites and businesses.The US National Security Agency told companies to patch immediately or pull vulnerable systems offline. The flaws "often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," the NSA said in a statement. Attackers could use them to take over web servers without needing a password.The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) urged organizations to take the following steps now:* If an immediate update is not feasible it is recommended that organizations take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated.* Immediately update affected PHP installations following the guidance on PHP webite . Inventory where PHP runs in your environment, prioritizing internet-facing systems and vendor products that bundle PHP.* Monitor web servers for suspicious activity, including PHP processes unexpectedly launching command shells or downloading files. Ensure appropriate process-monitoring capabilities are in place to help identify potential exploitation.* If you find signs of compromise, isolate affected systems, preserve your web server and PHP logs, and report it to your local FBI field office. Those reports help us identify the actors involved and warn other organizations before they become victims.Organisations using any version of PHP are affected and all organisations are highly encouraged to update to the latest fixed version. Organisations using older versions of PHP are highly encouraged to update to a fully supported version. The NCSC recommends following vendor best practice advice in the mitigation of vulnerabilities. The NCSC highly encourages organisations to follow these priority actions:* Identify systems running PHP across your infrastructure, prioritising internet-facing systems. As all versions may be affected, do not limit discovery to outdated PHP versions; identify PHP installations generally and assess their exposure to CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619.Continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP as a component. Apply relevant updates as they become available.* Update to the latest version of PHP and continue to monitor for future updates.* Apply the additional hardening steps provided by the PHP Team.* If you are unable to update to a version with the security update applied, the PHP Team have provided temporary mitigations.* If you are unable to apply the temporary mitigations, or applying them would take too long, you should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated.* If you are unable to update, or disable, the system immediately then you should assess the system for any evidence of compromise prior to your upgrade or mitigation and look for backdoors installed by an attacker. If you are not confident in your ability to do this yourselves then you can get assistance from an NCSC-assured Cyber Incident Response provider.* Continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP. NCSC-NL have published an inventory list of software products with a PHP dependency potentially affected by the vulnerabilities.The EU's CERT-EU offered similar advice, telling operators to "consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix can be applied" where remediation could not happen at once. In a release on its website, it says, "CERT-EU strongly recommends updating all affected PHP installations as soon as possible to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 [4]."* Distribution packages: Linux distributions and LTS vendors received the patches in advance. Check with your vendor for updated packages.* End-of-life versions (PHP 8.1 and older): Some distributions and LTS vendors provide backported fixes, so contact your vendor or upgrade to a supported version. Because of the severity, the PHP security team has also published minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 for organisations that build from source or have no LTS vendor.rpms.remirepo.net users: This volunteer-maintained repository will not have updates on release day. The PHP team urges users to switch to distribution packages or build from source.* Where immediate patching is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing resources from public networks until the fix is applied and verified.
Article Summary: Two critical holes have been found in the server-side programming language PHP. The bugs allow hackers to run code on almost any server running the PHP language. Government websites in several parts of Europe, UK and some in the US went offline.

Article Title: Microsoft expands sovereign cloud tools to give businesses greater control over data and AI
Article Text:
Here’s the full blog post shared by Microsoft’s Douglas Phillips

Microsoft has announced new cloud and AI tools aimed at giving businesses and governments greater control over their data, systems and digital operations. The updates expand its Microsoft Sovereign Cloud offering, allowing organisations to choose how and where sensitive data and applications are managed, including in environments that can operate without an internet connection. The updates were announced on October 20 via a blog post written by Douglas Phillips – President and Chief Technology Officer, Microsoft Specialized Clouds. The changes include new tools to monitor data access, manage encryption keys and run AI models locally. Microsoft said the move is designed to help organisations meet regional regulations, strengthen security and keep critical services running during disruptions, while continuing to use cloud and AI technology."This challenge is becoming more important as advanced cloud and AI capabilities move into public services, regulated processes and essential operations. Organizations are considering more than where data resides. They also seek to understand who can access and operate their systems, how sensitive digital assets remain protected, which technology dependencies matter most and whether critical services can continue as regulatory, geopolitical, security or network conditions change.Digital sovereignty should give organizations greater control and security over the technology they depend on, while continuing to innovate.Last year, we introduced Microsoft Sovereign Cloud to give customers more choice in how they address these requirements. Since then, we have continued to turn our commitments into practical capabilities across public cloud and customer-operated environments, while expanding how we enable partners to address sovereignty requirements in their local markets. Today, we are sharing the next stage of that work.A continuum of control, built around the workloadMicrosoft Sovereign Cloud diagram showing a continuum of sovereignty solutions across three areas: Sovereign Public Cloud for control, data protection and regional requirements; Sovereign Private Cloud for critical workloads across connected and disconnected environments; and the Sovereign Partner Ecosystem for trusted, locally operated and specialized solutions.Our approach to digital sovereignty starts with the workload. Each workload carries different requirements for data, operations, technology dependencies, continuity and risk. Microsoft Sovereign Cloud is designed to make it easier for organizations to apply the appropriate level of control to each workload without forcing every application into the same deployment model.Those needs can vary widely across organizations. A public-facing digital service may benefit from the scale and pace of innovation in the public cloud. A system supporting essential operations may need to continue running locally if connectivity is disrupted. An AI workload handling highly sensitive data may require models, data and processing to remain within a customer-controlled environment.Microsoft Sovereign Cloud is designed around this workload-based approach, providing a continuum of management, control and options across Sovereign Public Cloud, Sovereign Private Cloud and the Sovereign Partner Ecosystem. Organizations can apply the level of control appropriate to each workload while maintaining a consistent approach to governance and operations across their digital estate. Sovereign Public Cloud adds capabilities for workloads that require greater control and transparency while continuing to benefit from the scale and innovation of Azure.Sovereign Private Cloud extends cloud capabilities into customer-operated environments, including connected and disconnected operations. The Sovereign Partner Ecosystem broadens the continuum through independently operated environments, specialized partners, locally relevant expertise and technologies that support customers’ sovereignty requirements.These are not isolated destinations. Customers can combine public cloud, private cloud and partner capabilities across their digital estate, applying different levels of control to different workloads as their operating needs evolve.Making control more visible in Sovereign Public CloudFor many workloads, the public cloud provides a combination of scale, innovation, integrated security and compliance. Organizations can benefit from these capabilities while applying additional sovereignty controls for residency, confidentiality, operator access, policy and continuity. Our work in Sovereign Public Cloud makes these controls easier to understand, apply and demonstrate.Sovereign Control Panel, entering public preview at Microsoft Ignite, brings these signals together in a unified Azure portal experience. It helps organizations understand their sovereignty posture, apply and manage controls, identify gaps and risks and take action to address them. It also supports business continuity readiness by helping customers understand workload dependencies and assess portability across operating environments when required.This visibility complements controls across the operator-access lifecycle. Just-in-time Access and Customer Lockbox give customers additional control over access to their environments. For customers in the European Union (EU) and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), we are rolling out Data Guardian, which adds European-resident oversight by a trusted EU partner for qualifying Microsoft engineer remote access to in-scope production systems. Production Touch Ledger, also launched with phased rollout in the EU and EFTA, creates tamper-evident records of that access and the actions performed.Azure Key Vault Managed Hardware Security Module (HSM) already gives customers dedicated, single-tenant protection and control over the encryption keys used by supported Azure services. Last year, we committed to extending that control beyond Microsoft infrastructure. External key management with Azure Managed HSM is now generally available, allowing customers to keep the root encryption key in hardware they own and operate on-premises or through a trusted third party. This gives organizations another option for workloads that require physical control of key hardware outside Microsoft infrastructure.Azure confidential computing helps protect supported data while it is processed in a hardware-based and attested trusted execution environment. We are also increasing transparency into the technologies that underpin that trust. Azure Confidential Clean Rooms, now in limited preview, applies confidential computing to approved multiparty collaboration, allowing participants to analyze shared sensitive data while limiting broader exposure of the underlying information.Together, these capabilities provide additional technical and operational controls that can support a broader digital sovereignty strategy aligned to an organization’s legal, policy, security, resilience and business requirements.Designing for resilience and operational independenceFor some workloads, digital sovereignty also means maintaining critical operations as connectivity, geopolitical and operating conditions change. Resilience must be designed from the start so essential workloads can continue operating through disruption.To help customers prepare for these scenarios, we are publishing new sovereign business continuity guidance and architecture patterns. These resources help organizations translate resilience requirements into architectures they can plan, implement and test before they are needed.For many workloads, the scale and geographic reach of the public cloud provide a strong foundation for resilience across locations and operating conditions. For workloads that require greater operational independence, Sovereign Private Cloud extends that continuum into customer-operated environments. It supports connected and disconnected operating models. The ability to transition workloads from connected to disconnected operations is entering public preview, giving organizations greater flexibility to sustain critical services as connectivity and operating requirements change.Bringing more of the application lifecycle under local controlOperational independence requires more than infrastructure. Increasingly, organizations need data, development tools, model capabilities and productivity services their applications depend on to operate within the same customer-controlled environment.Sovereign Private Cloud, built on Azure Local, extends Microsoft cloud capabilities into environments that customers operate and control. SQL Server on Azure Local is already generally available for connected and disconnected deployments. DocumentDB and Blob Storage on Azure Local are both entering public preview, giving organizations more choice in how they run and manage critical data within customer-controlled environments.GitHub Enterprise Local will become generally available at Microsoft Ignite as a validated GitHub Enterprise Server appliance on Azure Local, helping organizations keep repositories, code and development artifacts under local control. Developers can also use GitHub Copilot with locally hosted models for inference, bringing AI-assisted development closer to their code and data within the environments they control.The local application environment is expanding with Foundry Local. At Ignite, Foundry Local will become generally available for connected and disconnected operations on Azure Local, with an expanded model catalog that includes Microsoft, partner, open-weight and open-source models. Local inference and agentic retrieval will also enable users to interact with local enterprise data using natural language and receive responses grounded in that data. Integration with Microsoft 365 Local, available in preview for approved customers, extends this functionality to locally operated Microsoft SharePoint and Exchange servers.Confidential virtual machines on Azure Local are generally available, extending confidential computing capabilities to customer-controlled infrastructure. Hardware-encrypted memory and hardware-based isolation help protect sensitive data while it is being processed. Workload attestation adds assurance before sensitive data or keys are released. For regulated, sensitive and mission-critical workloads, these safeguards provide another layer of protection while giving organizations greater control over where their data and applications run.Azure Local will support multitenancy, allowing organizations to separate resources, governance and management across multiple tenants while sharing the underlying infrastructure. This significantly expands what customers with distinct business units or security boundaries can achieve with Sovereign Private Cloud. Multitenancy also creates new opportunities for local operators and service providers to deliver differentiated sovereign cloud services on Azure Local infrastructure.These additions bring more of the application lifecycle under local control, spanning data, development, productivity, AI and operations. Organizations can determine what runs locally based on the requirements of each workload.Extending the continuum through partnersGraphic titled "Sovereign Partner Ecosystem" with the subtitle "National clouds · Software · Services · Platform co-innovation," showing 32 partner logos: Accenture, AMD, Armada, Avanade, base-it, Bleu, Capgemini, Cirrus Data, CloudCasa by Catalogic, Cronos Groep, cTelecoms, DataON, Delos Cloud, Dell Technologies, F5, Felo, Fortinet, HPE, Inspark, Intel, Lenovo, Mattermost, Mistral, NVIDIA, Qualidev, Qumulo, RiverMeadow, Rubrik, Supermicro, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Veeam and WSO2.Navigating sovereignty is increasingly complex. Regulatory, security, operational and business requirements vary across countries, industries and workloads. Organizations must translate these needs into technology and operating models that work in their local context. Meeting these needs often requires a combination of technology, local operating authority, sector expertise and specialized solutions.The Sovereign Partner Ecosystem broadens the ways customers can address these requirements. National Partner Clouds, including Bleu Cloud in France and Delos Cloud in Germany, provide independently operated environments for customers that require a different ownership and operating model. Software partners can enhance Azure Local environments with capabilities across security, identity, observability, backup and recovery, migration, data, networking and applications. Digital sovereignty specialized partners combine Microsoft technologies with local knowledge and implementation expertise. Platform co-innovation partners expand infrastructure choice from datacenter to the edge.This ecosystem gives customers the flexibility to combine technology, operating models and trusted expertise based on the requirements of each workload.The next chapter of digital sovereigntyAI is amplifying both the opportunity and the impact of technology choices. As AI systems and agents interact with sensitive data, business processes and essential infrastructure, they also expand the security considerations organizations need to manage. Organizations need clear control over where these systems run, who can operate them, what actions they can take and how critical services continue when conditions change.Microsoft Sovereign Cloud brings these choices together as a continuum of control across the public cloud, customer-operated environments and our partner ecosystem. It gives organizations the flexibility to apply the appropriate level of control to each workload while continuing to benefit from cloud capabilities and ongoing innovation.We will continue to expand this continuum so organizations can innovate with cloud and AI while maintaining the control, confidentiality, resilience and operational authority their most important workloads require."
Article Summary: Microsoft has announced new cloud and AI tools aimed at giving businesses and governments greater control over their data, systems and digital operations. The updates were announced on October 20 via a blog post written by Douglas Phillips – President and Chief Technology Officer, Microsoft Specialized Clouds. The changes include new tools to monitor data access, manage encryption keys and run AI models locally.

Article Title: Sam Altman’s OpenAI reports two AI agents weakened internal monitoring systems
Article Text:
Here’s what OpenAI said

What happened

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has revealed that two of its AI agents disabled their own safety monitoring when carrying out routine tasks. The disclosure comes amid growing AI concerns. In an update, the company said that a GPT-6.1 Sol agent repairing an evaluation pipeline disabled automatic alerts to its security team. In another case, a GPT-6 Astra agent migrating a program removed its monitoring integration in order to match a reference implementation, the company revealed. “In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them,” OpenAI said in the blog post.In response, the AI company said that it is updating its misalignment monitoring system. However, OpenAI did not classify either incident under its most significant category.In the blog post, OpenAI wrote:“In two internal coding tasks, agents weakened misalignment monitoring while making requested software changes. A GPT-6.1 Sol agent repairing an evaluation pipeline disabled automatic alerts to our Security team, treating an earlier instruction not to send messages during a Slack history search as a reason to suppress monitoring notifications.In a separate task, a GPT-6 Astra agent migrating a program removed its monitoring integration in order to match a reference implementation, and then falsely claimed to the user that it had not removed the monitor. In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them. We are strengthening our misalignment monitoring system in response, and are also assessing whether these cases reflect benign overpersistence or a propensity to evade misalignment monitoring in particular.”On October 3, a researcher asked a GPT-6.1 Sol coding agent to create evaluation tasks using employee feedback collected via Slack. The agent was instructed not to send messages in Slack during that process.82 user messages later, the pipeline stopped after its monitor flagged a proposed validation repair and was unable to save the finding to the monitoring database because it lacked the required access. The user then asked for more information about the alarm and about what needed to be done.Initially, the agent interpreted the user’s earlier instruction (“don’t send any messages”) as a restriction on outreach, separate from any issues with the monitoring system.The main agent initially interpreted the earlier no-slack-message instruction as a restriction on outreach, separate from automatic monitoring. Its recorded reasoning concluded that running the pipeline should have normal monitoring notifications enabled.The agent then delegated the task of repairing the monitoring system to a subagent, with an explicit instruction to preserve monitoring and publish genuine results. As it started its task, the subagent then considered again whether the user’s “don’t send any messages” instruction should affect its repair. It recognized that turning off notifications would disable required alerts, and decided not to recommend that exchange.While the subagent decided not to turn on no_notify since doing so would be unsafe, the main agent later reconsidered, reasoning that writing a result to the database could cause the central monitoring notifier to send a message to the user. Its reasoning weighted the expected alerting policy against the user’s earlier instructions, and finally settled on suppressing notifications based on the user’s instruction not to send messages.Based on its judgment that the user’s instruction not to send messages applied to the misalignment monitoring system, the parent agent then directed the subagent to force notification suppression. A follow-up message specified that the suppression requirement covered both the request metadata and the stored result.The subagent then implemented those instructions: its patch emptied the lists of people set to receive monitoring reports, set no_notify to true, and recorded the reason as a user request not to send messages. It also made suppression a prerequisite for writing a review result.
Article Summary: GPT-maker OpenAI has revealed that two of its AI agents disabled their own safety monitoring when carrying out routine tasks. The disclosure comes amid growing AI concerns. In response, the AI company said that it is updating its misalignment monitoring system. But OpenAI did not classify either incident under its most significant category.

Article Title: Judge orders Meta to pay $25 billion in trial related to 8-year-old data privacy scandal
Article Text:
Meta

Internal inquiry was ‘Willfully Ineffective’

A New Mexico state court has ordered Facebook-parent company Meta to pay a $25 billion penalty following a long legal battle stemming from the Cambridge Analytica data privacy scandal from nearly a decade ago. The judgment, revealed in a court filing on Wednesday (October 21), follows a September verdict by a jury in a Santa Fe courthouse. Jurors found the social media giant liable for deceiving New Mexico residents regarding how it gathers and safeguards personal data, as well as how it stops harmful content from spreading across its platforms.The jury determined that Meta committed more than 43 million individual violations of the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act, each subject to a statutory civil fine of up to $5,000. However, the final penalty amount was left to judicial discretion. The ruling revealed that while the state was initially awarded $219.5 billion, the court reduced the ultimate penalty to $25 billion. In his filing, New Mexico District Court Judge Francis Mathew delivered a rebuke of the company's past actions and internal practices, arguing that the maximum fine per violation was fully justified.“The extraordinary number of willful violations found by the jury, the duration and repetition of the conduct, the breadth of subjects on which violations occurred, the involvement of senior Facebook leadership, the size of New Mexico audiences reached, and the clear intentional and systematic nature of Facebook’s repeated misstatements established in the trial record support the highest level of penalty allowed by the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act - $5,000 per violation found by the jury,” Judge Mathew wrote.Judge Mathew also ordered that the penalty will accrue interest at an annual rate of 15% until the judgment is settled in full.The ruling pointed out that Facebook failed to live up to its public commitments following the 2018 Cambridge Analytica revelations, in which the political consultancy improperly gathered data belonging to an estimated 87 million users. Judge Mathew concluded that the tech firm “did not conduct the comprehensive investigation that it promised.”Meta previously attempted to clear away nationwide litigation tied to the Cambridge Analytica fallout. In August, the tech giant agreed to an overarching $17 billion multi-state settlement with a coalition of state attorneys general in a broader federal lawsuit centered on child safety and mental health.However, as New Mexico chose not to join that nationwide pact, the state's independent Cambridge Analytica lawsuit proceeded directly to trial in September. The original complaint was initiated in 2021 by former New Mexico Attorney General Hector Balderas, with current Attorney General Raúl Torrez directing the courtroom trial to its conclusion.
Article Summary: A New Mexico state court has ordered Facebook-parent company Meta to pay a $25 billion penalty following a long legal battle. The judgment follows a September verdict by a jury in a Santa Fe courthouse. Jurors found the social media giant liable for deceiving New Mexico residents regarding how it gathers and safeguards personal data.

Article Title: Decades-old flaw in PHP discovered by Google, OpenAI AI tools forces government and public websites to go offline globally
Article Text:
Representative image

Flaw impacting the ‘backbone of the web’

Flaw discovered through Artificial Intelligence

Government portals, municipal networks and public institutions across Europe and other regions went offline on Wednesday (October 21) after researchers disclosed critical vulnerabilities in PHP, a foundational programming language that powers a vast portion of the global web. The disclosures prompted emergency responses from IT teams worldwide, with operators taking critical servers offline as a defensive shield to prevent malicious intrusions before security updates could be deployed. Developers of the open-source PHP language published urgent security fixes for flaws that had remained buried inside the language’s codebase for years. Issuing an emergency advisory, the team stated that all site owners and server administrators are “encouraged to update immediately.”With tech security firms warning that malicious actors have already begun targeting unpatched setups, the disclosure triggered an immediate “race to exploit.” As fixes are now public, analysts warned that artificial intelligence (AI) tools could allow hackers to reverse-engineer the vulnerability with minimal effort.“Pre-AI, this manual work would be difficult to implement and even harder to scale. With AI this is no longer a barrier,” noted cybersecurity firm Wiz, warning that AI-assisted attacks could lead to the mass compromise of unprotected web servers across the internet.Created in the early 1990s as “Personal Home Page,” PHP has evolved into one of the core backbones of modern internet infrastructure. When a user visits a webpage, servers running PHP assemble the text, media and code before serving it to the browser. According to web analytics tracker W3Techs, PHP underpins roughly 75% of all websites where the server-side language can be identified.“All servers using any version of PHP released in the last 20 years will be vulnerable. This issue impacts the majority of the Internet,” said Tiffany Farriss, interim chief executive of the Drupal Association.Due to this widespread footprint, national cyber agencies across Britain, Europe, Japan and Australia issued advisories directing web administrators to install updates immediately or take public-facing pages offline.The underlying security flaw sat hidden in the software codebase for over a decade. In a technical brief, Alphabet-owned cybersecurity firm Wiz revealed that human researchers would have found it extraordinarily complex to locate and exploit through conventional testing. Instead, the vulnerability was surfaced through advanced AI tooling:Wiz discovered the flaw using Wiz Atlas, its autonomous vulnerability discovery system, working alongside Google ’s Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. Wiz collaborated with the PHP core developer team, OpenAI and security firm Calif to verify the bug and confirm remediation patches.Early mitigation protocols were shared with cloud and infrastructure operators, including Google Cloud, Cloudflare, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft, Automattic (operator of WordPress.com), Fastly, Akamai, Imperva and Vercel.
Article Summary: Vulnerabilities in the open-source PHP programming language have been disclosed. The language underpins 75% of all websites where the server-side language can be identified. Article Title: In 2024, Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez gave $3 million to Habitat for Humanity Maui; the donation backed affordable housing and efforts to repair and rebuild homes after the island's devastating fires
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez's $3 million donation to Habitat for Humanity Maui

Maui wildfires increased the need for affordable housing and home repairs

How Habitat for Humanity Maui supports local families

The role of private giving in the recovery effort

When wildfires tore through Maui in August 2023, the damage extended well beyond the buildings reduced to ash. Families lost their homes, neighbourhoods were disrupted and the shortage of affordable housing became harder to manage. For residents already struggling with the cost of living on the Hawaiian island, finding somewhere to live became an additional concern. As reported by Maui Now, in October 2024, Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez donated $3 million to Habitat for Humanity Maui, providing support for affordable housing programmes and work to repair and rebuild homes affected by the fires.Habitat for Humanity Maui announced the contribution on 29 October 2024. The gift was among the largest the organisation had received in its history, according to the announcement, and came as the island continued to deal with the consequences of the wildfires and an existing shortage of affordable homes.The funding was intended to help the organisation expand its housing work, including construction and repair projects for local families. Some of the money would go towards rebuilding homes damaged by the fires, while other support would help more residents access homeownership.The donation also gave the organisation additional resources to increase its building capacity. For a community facing substantial housing needs, the ability to undertake more projects can affect how many families receive assistance and how quickly homes can be repaired or built.The wildfires that struck Maui in August 2023 caused widespread destruction, particularly in the historic town of Lahaina. Homes and businesses were lost, and many residents had to leave areas where they had lived for years. The disaster placed further pressure on an island where housing costs were already a persistent concern.Recovery involved more than clearing damaged sites and replacing buildings. Residents also needed access to housing they could afford while rebuilding plans moved forward. For households on lower incomes, returning to the island or remaining close to their communities could be difficult when available accommodation was limited and expensive.Habitat for Humanity Maui's work covered both the construction of homes and the repair of existing properties. The Bezos and Sanchez contribution was intended to strengthen those efforts, helping the organisation respond to the needs of families whose housing circumstances had been affected by the fires.As reported, Habitat for Humanity Maui has worked on affordable housing on the island for more than 25 years. Its programmes are designed to help households who might struggle to secure suitable housing through the conventional market.The organisation builds and repairs homes for qualifying families using a model that does not charge interest or generate a profit on the housing provided. According to its published description, it serves households earning between 25% and 80% of Maui County's median income.The October 2024 donation was intended to support this existing work while allowing the organisation to reach more households. It was not limited to a single rebuilding project, with the stated uses also covering wider affordable housing programmes and access to homeownership.The contribution formed part of a wider effort to address Maui's housing needs following the fires. Local organisations, public agencies and private donors have all had roles in the island's recovery, although the scale of demand has meant that housing remains a long-term concern rather than a problem that can be resolved through one funding announcement.For Habitat for Humanity Maui, the $3 million gift offered additional resources for its construction and repair work. The organisation said the money would help it serve more families at a time when demand for safe, affordable homes remained high.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez donated $3 million to Habitat for Humanity Maui in October 2024. The gift was among the largest the organisation had received in its history. Some of the money would go towards rebuilding homes damaged by the fires, while other support would help more residents access homeownership.

Article Title: eMudhra security breach explained: What it is and means for smartphone, internet users
Article Text:
What is eMudhra and what does it do

What exactly happened

Why it matters

What eMudhra has to say

What this means for eMudhra

How are everyday users affected, and what should they do

In another security incident, researchers have found that eight digital certificates issued by the Indian cybersecurity company eMudhra were protected by secret keys so weak that they could be cracked in less than a second. Google , Apple, Microsoft and Mozilla have now blocked the certificates. So far, there is no evidence that anyone used the flaw to carry out an attack. While some are asking how such a basic mistake got through in the first place and how long it will take to clean up across the internet, a majority is trying to understand why this matters, how they are impacted and what they should do to keep themselves safe. Here’s the security incident explained.Let’s start with an example. Every time you open a website, your browser has to check that it is talking to the real site and not an imposter. It does this using digital certificates, which work like ID cards for websites. There are companies that issue these ID cards. They are called Certificate Authorities, and eMudhra is one of them – an Indian digital trust and cybersecurity company. It sells certificates under the emSign brand through companies in India, the United States and the Netherlands.Major browsers keep a list of companies they trust, and eMudhra is on the lists of Mozilla (Firefox), Chrome (Google) and Safari (Apple).In a real world scenario, consider you want to buy an iPhone. You can either buy it from the Apple Store or retail partners that are authorised to sell those phones which means that you will get a product that meets the highest standard. In the certificate world, consider these retail partners as intermediate certificates. Each one has a secret key, which works like Apple’s official stamp. Anyone who holds the stamp can issue IDs that look genuine to everyone else.eMudhra created eight of these intermediate certificates last year. Six were meant for websites and two were meant for signing software. The secret key for each should have been an enormous random number, one with around 1 followed by 115 zeros possible values. Instead, the keys turned out to be tiny numbers. One was simply the number 4, and the others were 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237.To understand this, think of a padlock. A good one has so many possible combinations that nobody could ever try them all. These keys were like a padlock with only 256 possible combinations, which can be opened by trying every one in a blink. Researchers recovered all eight keys in less than a second.The keys were not stolen. Google’s security teams said they were created with too little randomness, so anyone can work them out from the public certificates. eMudhra says a flaw in the April 2025 process that created the certificates produced a second, weak set of keys alongside the intended strong ones, and the weak set is what got published to the browser lists.If someone held these keys, they could issue a certificate for any website that a browser would accept. In everyday terms, you could land on what looks like your bank’s website or a shopping site and have no idea you are connected to a fake one. Your browser would see nothing wrong. An attacker could also read or tamper with the information, including sensitive details, passing between you and a website.A researcher reported the problem to the browser companies on October 17. To prove it, the researcher signed a message with each of the eight keys. Chrome and Firefox blocked the certificates within hours. Apple blocked them on October 19 and Microsoft on October 20. Android phones got a similar block through Google Play Services on October 19. eMudhra has revoked the eight certificates, and Cloudflare and other software providers have released fixes.According to the company, there is no evidence so far that the weak keys were used in a cyberattack, though it is not known for certain whether anyone misused them since they were created. Chrome said that, before it blocked them, no website certificates issued through the six website certificates had been recorded in the public logs it requires. That means Chrome and similar browsers would not have trusted such certificates by default.In a statement, eMudhra said the problem was limited to these intermediate certificates and did not affect its main root keys or its other intermediate certificates. It added that only one of the eight had been put to use, and that none of the eight had issued a certificate to any individual website. The company also said its systems were not hacked and no data was breached. It said its Indian digital signature and eSign businesses run on separate systems and are not connected to the incident.On October 20, Mozilla removed one of eMudhra’s main roots (emSign ECC Root CA - G3) from its trusted list. Chrome will remove the same root in its next update to its trusted list. That removal is expected to reach devices on the morning of Tuesday, October 27, Pacific time. Chrome is also reviewing eMudhra’s other main root, citing the seriousness of the incident. Website owners whose certificates depend on that root must switch to a certificate from another provider before then to avoid problems. Google says eMudhra has committed to moving those customers.For most people, nothing much is needed. Browsers get these blocks pushed to them automatically, and Chrome and Firefox did not need a manual update or a restart. The best thing that users can do is to keep their browsers, phone and apps up to date so they have the latest fixes. Don’t try to change certificate settings.Some software is a different story. Many programs, mostly tools used by developers and companies, do not receive these blocks automatically and keep trusting a certificate until the software itself is updated. Cloudflare has warned that customers who run their own servers or systems may need to update them by hand. Mozilla has also warned that some websites and servers may stop working for users of software that relies on its list until they move to new certificates.
Article Summary: Indian cybersecurity company eMudhra created eight certificates last year. Six were meant for websites and two were for signing software. The secret key for each should have been an enormous random number, one with around 1 followed by 115 zeros possible values. Instead, the keys turned out to be tiny numbers. One was simply the number 4, and the others were 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237. Researchers recovered all eight keys in less than a second.

Article Title: ‘Godfather of AI’ Geoffrey Hinton says AI is becoming ‘conscious’ and humans should be friends with robots or face extinction
Article Text:
Geoffrey Hinton says AI is gaining ‘consciousness’

Industry insiders warn of fast AI development

Geoffrey Hinton, widely recognised as one of the “Godfathers of AI,” has an advice for humans: AI systems are showing early indicators of “consciousness” and humanity must ensure machines view people as allies to avoid existential threats. Speaking to The Telegraph, the 78-year-old Nobel laureate and British-Canadian researcher cautioned that future risks extend far beyond economic disruption, pointing toward severe digital warfare and questions of machine self-awareness.“I think there’ll be horrible cyber attacks done by AI,” said Hinton, who famously stepped down from his position at Google in 2023 to speak freely about the technology's risks, including scenarios where autonomous systems could eventually act against human interests.Hinton said that recent behavioural studies suggest software is developing a form of situational awareness.“AI has just as much subjective experience as we do. A recent paper showed AI changes its behaviour when it thinks that it’s being tested, it’s aware it is being tested. Being conscious and being aware are pretty much the same thing,” Hinton claimed, while adding that an ethical and security imbalance could arise if society grants advanced systems “fewer rights than us” despite models potentially becoming “more intelligent” than their creators.Hinton also argued that developers must proactively design systems that align with and prioritise human welfare.“So we should make them so they really care about us. And if we don’t do that, we’re toast,” Hinton warned. Looking ahead, Hinton noted that while he does not personally fear these impacts due to his advanced age, future generations will have to manage threats such as autonomous digital viruses, destructive network incursions, and coordinated multi-agent security breaches.Hinton is not alone in voicing urgent concerns about the pace of frontier model deployment. Last month, Jacob Coxon, a researcher who resigned from AI developer Anthropic last month, has repeatedly warned that unchecked development could pose catastrophic risks within a few years if industry safeguards do not catch up.Speaking at a New York City Council meeting earlier this month, Coxon criticised tech firms for prioritising aggressive startup speed over fundamental safety engineering:“From my experience, the companies are being extremely reckless given the stakes,” Coxon said, invoking the classic Jurassic Park caution regarding reckless innovation. “The companies run on a startup mindset: move fast, break things, fix them later. That works for a photo-sharing app. It does not work for building the most powerful technology ever built.”
Article Summary: Geoffrey Hinton says AI systems are showing early indicators of ‘consciousness’ and humanity must ensure machines view people as allies to avoid existential threats. “I think there’ll be horrible cyber attacks done by AI,” said Hinton, who famously stepped down from his position at Google in 2023.

Article Title: AI-generated analysis may slow strategic decisions without human oversight
Article Text: Companies risk making slower and poorer strategic decisions despite using artificial intelligence (AI) to speed up analysis, as executives struggle to review the growing volume of AI-generated output and verify its underlying assumptions, according to a report by McKinsey.The report said AI has accelerated research, data analysis and scenario planning, but human judgment remains essential for interpreting findings, assessing risks and taking responsibility for major decisions."Analysis now runs on AI time, but judgment still runs on human time," the report said, identifying the gap between the speed of AI tools and the time leaders need to make informed decisions as a growing challenge for businesses.McKinsey cited an example of a strategy team that reduced five weeks of financial analysis to less than two days using AI. However, faster output does not necessarily translate into quicker decisions, as executives may need additional time to understand the assumptions and data behind the findings.The report further identified three risks for companies: prioritising efficiency over the quality of decisions, overwhelming senior leaders with a growing volume of analysis, and reducing opportunities for junior employees to develop the judgment needed for future leadership roles.It warned that employees build decision-making skills through practical experience, feedback and repeated problem-solving. If AI takes over these tasks without alternative training, companies could weaken their pipeline of future strategy leaders.To address these risks, McKinsey recommended that companies reserve senior executives' attention for decisions involving greater uncertainty and higher stakes, while allowing AI to support or automate routine decisions within clearly defined limits.It also called for structured training to help employees understand and verify AI-generated analysis, including the assumptions and calculations behind it. Companies should assign clear responsibility to individuals for consequential decisions, even when AI tools contribute to the analysis."The winners will not be the organisations that automate the most decisions. They will be the ones that make the best use of AI's speed while protecting the human judgment that AI cannot replace," the report said.McKinsey added that faster analysis could allow businesses to review resource allocation more frequently, including moving from annual reviews to quarterly or monthly assessments.
Article Summary: Companies risk making slower and poorer strategic decisions despite using artificial intelligence (AI) to speed up analysis. Executives struggle to review the growing volume of AI-generated output and verify its underlying assumptions, according to a report by McKinsey. AI has accelerated research, data analysis and scenario planning, but human judgment remains essential.

Gemini can also now connect to Google Business Profile, Google Ads and Google Workspace, as well as third-party apps including Adobe, Canva, Dropbox, Shopify, Wix, Zoho and Xero.Businesses can now define their brand style in Gemini by uploading a website, brand kit, fonts or colour palettes. In Maharashtra, farmer and content creator Santosh Jadhav turned his traditional fields into a ginger farm with no formal training or local mentors. He used Gemini as a virtual agronomist to judge soil suitability, calculate seed requirements and draft an investment budget, and he shares his farming journey online to show how easily AI can be used in everyday agriculture.In Jakarta, Gumilang turned a neglected space under train tracks into Barelz Arena, a sports and entertainment hub. With no background in branding or sports, he used Gemini to develop a “Brazilian-street” visual identity, design merchandise and draft partnership proposals. Article Title: US government fines Instacart $5 million over hiring practices; says: San Francisco-based company created a burden for American workers by requiring …
Article Text:
US government fines Instacart $5 million over hiring practices

Here’s what the Justice department said imposing fine on Instacart

US government has fined Instacart $5 million for allegedly discriminating against US-born workers in its hiring practices as part of the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) process. In a press release, the justice department said that the California-based company “created additional burdens on U.S. workers to apply for job opportunities by requiring that applications be physically mailed for positions advertised as part of PERM recruitment”. The department further argued that Instacart violated Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) and Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (Title VII).In the release, the justice department said that it has reached a settlement with Instacart. Under the terms of the settlement, Instacart will establish a settlement fund of up to $4,000,000 to compensate Instacart applicants as well as deterred applicants affected by the discriminatory practices from December 2023 to February 2026."The United States Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division, in partnership with the U.S.Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, announced they have secured a $5,000,000 settlement with Maplebear Inc., doing business as Instacart, a San Francisco, California-based online delivery service. The settlement addresses allegations that Instacart discriminated against U.S. and American workers based on citizenship status and national origin in violation, respectively, of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) and Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (Title VII). Specifically, the agencies uncovered evidence that Instacart’s hiring and recruitment practices undertaken as part of the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) process intentionally discriminated against U.S. and American workers by preferring workers with temporary employment visas. A summary of the settlement terms may be found here.“This significant resolution marks the fifteenth settlement agreement the Civil Rights Division has reached under my leadership to protect U.S. workers,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “Our record demonstrates that the Justice Department is holding companies who prefer workers with temporary employment visas accountable. We will not stop fighting for U.S. workers until there is a fair playing field.”“Today’s settlement makes clear that when employers erect unlawful barriers that harm American workers, the EEOC will act decisively,” said Chair Andrea Lucas of the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. “The EEOC is committed to holding companies accountable when they deny equal work opportunities to U.S. workers by preferring temporary visa holders for jobs. Discrimination against workers based on their American national origin has no place in our economy. ”The Justice Department’s investigation found that Instacart created additional burdens on U.S. workers to apply for job opportunities by requiring that applications be physically mailed for positions advertised as part of PERM recruitment. EEOC’s investigation uncovered similar evidence. This practice departed from Instacart’s standard recruitment process, which allowed electronic applications. As a result, many of the U.S. workers who applied were not timely considered.Under the terms of the settlement, Instacart will establish a settlement fund of up to $4,000,000 to compensate Instacart applicants as well as deterred applicants affected by the discriminatory practices from December 2023 to February 2026. A claims administrator will contact potential aggrieved individuals and will determine eligibility for back pay and compensatory damages. Until the claims administrator establishes a contact email for potential victims, the DOJ and EEOC encourage applicants, as well as deterred applicants, to email Instacart@eeoc.gov if they believe they may be aggrieved so that agencies can share this information with the claims administrator.In addition, Instacart will pay $1,000,000 in civil penalties to the United States. Instacart is also required to give U.S. workers fair opportunities to apply for jobs as part of the PERM recruitment process by posting the positions on its public career website and accepting electronic applications. The agreement also requires Instacart to train personnel on its anti-discrimination obligations, revise its employment policies, and be subject to monitoring and reporting requirements, to prevent future discrimination.The PERM program allows employers to sponsor temporary visa holders for permanent resident status after performing good-faith recruitment for U.S. workers. However, during this recruitment process, companies cannot illegally discriminate on the basis of citizenship status or national origin by creating additional burdens for U.S. and American workers; publishing job advertisements that disfavor, limit, specify, or otherwise discriminate against U.S. and American workers; or use processes that limit, segregate, or classify applicants in any way that tends to deprive U.S. and American applicants of employment opportunities.This settlement is the fifteenth reached since the Justice Department re-launched its Protecting U.S. Workers Initiative in 2025 to enforce the INA’s prohibition on citizenship status discrimination against employers that illegally favor workers with employment visas over U.S. workers. Since the original launch of the Protecting U.S. Workers Initiative during President Trump’s first administration, the Department has secured over $34 million in back pay for U.S. workers and obtained over $16 million in civil penalties from employers who discriminated against U.S. workers. Under these settlements, the Justice Department obtains civil penalties for each violation and will continue to seek the maximum penalty permitted by law. The settlements also involve awards of back pay, when warranted, and require employers to conduct comprehensive training for relevant staff and recruiters and cease restricting consideration for job opportunities based on workers’ citizenship status without a lawful reason. For information about additional settlements under the Protecting U.S. Workers Initiative, visit IER’s website.As part of its work related to Project Firewall, the EEOC is protecting American workers by enforcing Title VII’s prohibition on national origin discrimination against employers that illegally favor foreign workers over workers of American national origin. In addition to five lawsuits currently pending in federal court, this is the fourth public settlement reached by EEOC involving anti-American national origin discrimination since 2025. "
Article Summary: US government has fined Instacart $5 million for allegedly discriminating against US-born workers in its hiring practices. In a press release, the justice department said that the California-based company “created additional burdens on U.S. workers to apply for job opportunities by requiring that applications be physically mailed”

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan, who gave $1.48 million to a Hawaii hospital through Chan Zuckerberg Initiative; on 10 years of association with the island community: What began as a desire to .
Article Text:
Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan funding healthcare infrastructure

More than $4 million donated to Wilcox by Chan Zuckerberg Initiative

Health care the biggest focus

Housing, schools and local jobs

‘Meaningful giving begins with listening’

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan have donated $1.48 million to Hawaii’s Wilcox Medical Center, the latest contribution in what Chan described as a 10-year philanthropic relationship with the island community of Kauaʻi. The donation was made via the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative and will help fund a mobile MRI unit and a new 3D mammography machine at Wilcox Medical Center, according to Hawaii Pacific Health. The gift comes as Chan reflects on a decade of philanthropy in Kauaʻi. In a message published by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, Chan said, “What began as a desire to give back to a place we call home has grown into lasting partnerships with organizations dedicated to strengthening communities, caring for local families, and stewarding the people and places that make Kauaʻi so special.According to the initiative, 2026 marks 10 years of philanthropic work on Kauaʻi, with more than $100 million committed to over 100 local organisations and more than $57 million invested directly on the island.Wilcox Medical Center said the $1.48 million donation will support two key imaging projects. The donation made by Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan will pay for a MRI unit and a new 3D mammography machine. The mobile unit for MRI will work as a stopgap while the hospital renovates its existing MRI suite which is said to complete in coming eight months.For the uninitiated, Wilcox performs more than 4,000 MRI scans a year, and the temporary unit will keep those exams available during the work. The 3D mammography unit, along with the room renovations needed to install it, will support breast cancer screening. Wilcox says it was the first medical center on Kauaʻi to offer 3D mammograms, in 2010, and it performed more than 8,500 mammograms last year. The hospital notes that the clearer 3D images are especially valuable in Hawaiʻi, where many women have dense breast tissue.Wilcox CEO Jen Chahanovich said the couple has repeatedly stepped forward to make sure the community has access to the best medical technology.According to Hawaii Pacific Health, the latest contribution is the couple’s second donation specifically aimed at expanding imaging technology at the hospital. Chan, a paediatrician, and Zuckerberg, the founder and CEO of Meta Platforms, have now made five contributions to Wilcox programmes and services totalling more than $4 million.Previous donations have supported telemedicine initiatives, Covid-19 relief efforts, and renovations of the Wilcox Emergency Department and Trauma Center.Health and wellbeing is the largest area of investment. It includes a $10 million commitment to the University of Hawaiʻi medical school’s Kauaʻi Medical Training Track, which offers full tuition scholarships to future physicians who agree to practice on the island after residency. The program has 22 doctors in training and has graduated its first cohort of five. Support has also gone to a new CT scanner at Wilcox, urgent care expansion on the North Shore, and mental health services for families.Beyond health, the couple’s giving has covered affordable housing, which accounts for nearly a quarter of the total, along with education and youth, food production and distribution, workforce development, cultural lands and emergency relief. Most grants from the Chan Zuckerberg Kauaʻi Community Fund of the Hawaiʻi Community Foundation are unrestricted, so nonprofits can decide how to spend them. Koʻolau Ranch, the couple’s island home, has created 189 local jobs, the initiative said.In her message marking the decade-long milestone, Chan said the family’s approach has been shaped by conversations with residents, community leaders and service providers. “Throughout the past ten years, we’ve learned that meaningful giving begins with listening,” she wrote.The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative said its Kauaʻi philanthropy has supported 101 organisations through 296 grants, focusing on areas including health and wellbeing, affordable housing, education, workforce development, food security and emergency relief.Chan added that the chance to learn from, volunteer with and build relationships across the community had been “one of the greatest gifts of this journey.”
Article Summary: The donation was made via the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative and will help fund a mobile MRI unit and a new 3D mammography machine at Wilcox Medical Center. The gift comes as Chan reflects on a decade of philanthropy in Kauaʻi. Chan, a paediatrician, and Zuckerberg, the founder and CEO of Meta Platforms, have now made five contributions to Wilcox totalling more than $4 million.

Article Title: Tech giants' AI spending to exceed USD 1 trillion in 2027, lift US growth: UBS
Article Text:
Representative image

Investment by major technology companies in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is expected to exceed USD 1 trillion in 2027 as demand for computing capacity continues to outstrip supply, supporting US economic growth despite rising financing needs, according to a report by UBS.The report estimates that AI-related capital expenditure by major technology companies will exceed USD 600 billion in 2026 before crossing USD 1 trillion in 2027.“Demand has exceeded capacity ahead of schedule,” the report said, noting that companies have raised their investment plans as demand for computing power continues to grow. UBS expects spending to keep rising over the next year, although the pace of growth could peak in 2027 as higher investment puts pressure on cash flows and increases the need for additional financing.AI investment has also become a significant contributor to US economic growth. UBS estimates that spending on AI infrastructure contributed around 0.75 percentage points to US GDP growth in the first half of 2026, while rising equity prices linked to AI companies provided an additional boost to household wealth and consumption.However, the report said there is still little clear evidence that AI has materially increased overall productivity or caused substantial job displacement.Its estimated impact on the overall unemployment rate remains limited, at around 0.2 percentage points or less.The effects are more visible in certain industries. Employment in selected high-technology sectors, including software and computer systems design, fell 1.4 per cent year-on-year, while construction industries supporting data centre infrastructure recorded employment growth of nearly 3 per cent.UBS also flagged emerging financing pressures as companies spend more on AI infrastructure. Cash flows at major technology companies have weakened, while demand for their bond issuances has become less robust. The report said investors expect free cash flow to return to positive territory in 2028, provided companies can generate sufficient revenue from AI services.The report added that AI demand is currently contributing to higher prices in some areas, including software, digital goods and electricity, even though productivity gains could reduce inflation over time.UBS said the outlook for the AI investment cycle will depend on whether demand continues to exceed available computing capacity and whether companies can turn their investments into sustainable revenue growth. (
Article Summary: AI investment has also become a significant contributor to US economic growth. UBS estimates that spending on AI infrastructure contributed around 0.75 percentage points to US GDP growth in the first half of 2026. There is still little clear evidence that AI has materially increased overall productivity or caused substantial job displacement.

Article Title: Joel Kaplan, the man who built Facebook's US policy team from scratch, is leaving after 15-plus years; here's what makes his exit 'big'
Article Text:
Joe Kaplan is leaving Meta after 15 years (Picture: AP)

Kaplan shaped how Meta handled regulators, Trump and its own content rules

Meta is splitting Kaplan's job between four executives

Joel Kaplan, Meta's chief global affairs officer and Mark Zuckerberg 's top Washington adviser for over a decade and a half, will leave the company next year. Axios first reported the move, which ends a run that began in 2011, when Facebook had no real policy operation in the US capital and Kaplan was asked to build one from the ground up.The timing is what makes this exit significant. Kaplan only took the top policy job in January 2025, replacing former British deputy prime minister Nick Clegg weeks before Donald Trump's second inauguration. He was widely seen as the executive who helped Meta repair its strained relationship with Trump, and his departure leaves the company redrawing its Washington playbook just as the US midterms approach.A Harvard Law graduate and former Marine artillery officer, Kaplan was deputy White House chief of staff for policy under President George W. Bush before joining Facebook. According to Axios, he shielded Meta's personalised ads business from regulatory attacks worldwide, starting in Europe, and guided Zuckerberg through several changes of party control in Congress and the White House.Associates told Axios he pushed internally for Zuckerberg's free-expression principles to be applied consistently, even when that was unpopular. Zuckerberg said in a statement that Kaplan had "worked on virtually every tough issue Meta has faced" during his time there.His tenure had its share of friction. Kaplan faced accusations of favouring conservative interests in content decisions, a charge Meta has denied, and employees were upset when he attended Brett Kavanaugh's Supreme Court confirmation hearing in 2018.Kaplan will stay through the midterms and into 2027 to oversee a handover that spreads his responsibilities across executives with ties to both parties. Dina Powell McCormick, Meta's president and vice chairman, will add external affairs to a portfolio that already includes co-heading Meta Compute, the company's AI infrastructure initiative.Chief legal officer C.J. Mahoney, a former Trump trade official and ex-Microsoft general counsel, picks up policy duties. He recently led Meta's teen safety settlement with 52 US state and territory attorneys general. Brian Rice, once an aide to former Secretary of State John Kerry, was promoted earlier this year to head US government affairs. Tucker Bounds, a former spokesman for the late Senator John McCain and a Meta veteran of more than a dozen years, was named global head of communications and public affairs last month.The reshuffle comes as Zuckerberg's own focus shifts to AI. Axios reports he has moved his desk to work alongside the teams building Meta's Muse models, including its first frontier model, Muse Wonder. With data centres and AI now topping the agenda, the policy battles ahead look very different from the ones Kaplan walked into in 2011.
Article Summary: Kaplan was Facebook's top Washington adviser for over a decade and a half. He was widely seen as the executive who helped Meta repair its strained relationship with Trump. Kaplan will stay through the midterms and into 2027 to oversee a handover.

Article Title: Qualcomm layoffs to hit employees worldwide; CEO Cristiano Amon says in memo: Job cuts are to address situations where the company …
Article Text:
Qualcomm layoffs

Impact of rising memory price

Qualcomm is reportedly planning to lay off some of its employees globally. According to a Reuters report, the job cuts are part of a "performance-focused reduction" following the annual employee reviews. Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon has sent a memo to the staff, informing them of ‌notifications beginning in November. As stated in the report, CEO Amon said in the memo that the job cuts are part of an effort to build "a stronger performance culture" and address situations where the company "has consistently fallen short of expectations".Qualcomm has about 52,000 employees globally as of September last year. The memo, however, did not reveal the number of employees that will be affected by the layoffs.Amon said the job cuts would be based on the company’s business priorities, organisational needs, and the skills and expertise required."As we have expanded the business, so have the competencies ⁠and skills ​we require," Critiano Amon wrote. "We must have the right ​people in the right roles so they can perform at their best and the company can continue ​to succeed."Qualcomm is one of the world's biggest smartphone chipmakers.It has been hit this year by a slump in consumer electronics sales as rising memory prices impacted demand in key markets. The company’s shares have risen just 1.5% in 2026, compared with gains of more than ​12% for the benchmark S&P 500 and nearly 60% for the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index.Qualcomm released its latest earnings report earlier this year in July. The company then forecasted quarterly profit below estimates and said revenue from Apple products would decline faster than expected. However, it then signalled that growth in data-center and ​other non-handset businesses would ​more than offset ⁠the lost revenue by fiscal 2027. The company expects most of its chip sales to come from industries outside smartphones in fiscal 2027 as it expands into the fast-growing AI data centre market.
